candidates.reason: PDF.js reproduces the source document's own page colors rather than application chrome.
candidates.boundaryDescription: Only pixels painted by PDF.js into each page canvas; selection, annotation, loading, error, toolbar, and signature-placement chrome remain governed application UI.

candidates.reason: The signature artifact must preserve dark ink on a paper surface when embedded into a document.
candidates.boundaryDescription: Only the signature canvas bitmap: the bg-white canvas and its 2D-context strokeStyle; dialog controls and surrounding borders remain governed application UI.

candidates.reason: The placed signature preview is document content and must match the captured signature artifact.
candidates.boundaryDescription: Only the generated signature-preview canvas pixels; placement handles, deletion controls, focus treatment, and annotation overlays are excluded.

candidates.reason: The QR module and quiet zone need fixed machine-readable contrast in the dark application theme.
candidates.boundaryDescription: Only the qrcode.react QRCodeSVG foreground/background and its immediate white quiet-zone container; pairing status, retry, instructions, and modal chrome remain governed UI.

candidates.reason: Shiki grammar scopes require the separately governed vitesse-dark syntax palette.
candidates.boundaryDescription: Only token colors generated inside ShikiHighlighter's highlighted code body; code-block header, copy state, border, background chrome, and prose remain governed UI.

candidates.reason: CodeMirror's oneDark grammar token colors form syntax content rather than application status chrome.
candidates.boundaryDescription: Only CodeMirror grammar-token spans supplied by theme=dark; selection, active-line, gutter, editor surface, borders, and focus chrome are excluded and must use tokens.

candidates.reason: Mermaid diagram nodes, edges, notes, pie series, and quadrant series use a separately governed visualization palette.
candidates.boundaryDescription: Only Mermaid configuration values and sanitized SVG diagram paint; loading/error chrome and surrounding code-block UI remain governed application UI. Activation requires D14 non-color series cues.

candidates.reason: Chart series may use the separately governed visualization palette when a second distinction channel is present.
candidates.boundaryDescription: Only SVG series strokes/fills and matching legend swatches indexed from SERIES_COLORS; axes, labels, empty states, and container chrome remain governed UI. Current hue-only multi-series output is not eligible for activation until D14's second cue is implemented.

candidates.reason: File-type indicators are explicitly included in the D14 separately governed encoding palette.
candidates.boundaryDescription: Only the file-type icon foreground and its derived 13-percent-alpha icon tile; filename, metadata, remove control, focus, border, and upload state remain governed UI.

candidates.reason: An agent color is selected by the user and persisted as agent data.
candidates.boundaryDescription: Only the persisted Agent.color value and its named palette choices; status, validation, selected-control, and surrounding card chrome are excluded.

candidates.reason: Palette swatches present and select the persisted agent-authored color value.
candidates.boundaryDescription: Only each swatch's backgroundColor sourced from AVATAR_COLORS; selection rings, labels, keyboard focus, validation, and form chrome remain governed UI.

candidates.reason: The avatar reproduces persisted Agent.color data.
candidates.boundaryDescription: Only the avatar disk backgroundColor when sourced from agent.color; card status, badges, actions, text, border, and fallback surface remain governed UI.

candidates.reason: The worker avatar reproduces persisted Agent.color data.
candidates.boundaryDescription: Only the avatar disk backgroundColor when sourced from agent.color; worker status and card chrome remain governed UI.

candidates.reason: The activity avatar reproduces the agent-selected color carried with activity data.
candidates.boundaryDescription: Only avatar backgroundColor sourced from item.agentColor; text/icon foreground, fallback, state indicators, and surrounding timeline chrome remain governed UI.

candidates.reason: Agent message avatars reproduce the selected agent color supplied by message data.
candidates.boundaryDescription: Only backgroundColor when the agentColor branch is selected; user-avatar accent treatment, foreground, message status, and message chrome remain governed UI.

candidates.reason: Search agent-group avatars reproduce persisted Agent.color data.
candidates.boundaryDescription: Only the AgentHeader avatar backgroundColor sourced from agent.color; result highlights, selection, status, text, focus, and modal chrome remain governed UI.

candidates.reason: Assigned-agent markers reproduce the selected agent color carried in graph node data.
candidates.boundaryDescription: Only assigned-agent avatar/icon paint sourced from data.agentColor; task status visual.color, node rails, dependency edges, badges, and graph chrome are explicitly excluded because they are application status or visualization semantics.

reviewedNonExceptions.reason: Application status chrome is governed by D3 semantic tokens and must never enter the visualization or user-authored exception categories.
Graph placement does not turn task lifecycle colors into a visualization exception; these values remain status chrome.
Low-level primitive implementation is an import-boundary concept, not a permanent color exception. Primitive sources still consume design-system tokens and receive no directory-wide exemption.
